title: The Shieldings' stone and the bargain contradict each other and the game never reconciles it. 'The Field's Stone' quest completes with 'You draft a line neither asked for and both can stand behind. Bevan cuts it; Ossett signs the wording' (a physical carved, signed stone). Minutes later, 'argue him off the warrant' (needed for the bargain's three refusals) resolves with 'Bevan sets his chisel down... it stays under canvas' and 'No stone was ever going to sit easy... not the Crown's, not anyone's' (no stone at all). The game lets both be true simultaneously with no bridging text, and the final epilogue enshrines the contradiction permanently: 'A third wording stands on the Shieldings' stone, the Crown's and the Companies' both, brokered rather than won.' immediately followed by 'No stone stands on the Shieldings at all. The field was given whole to its dead, and the fork said so plainly.'
where: The Stone-Cutter's Lodge (Bevan) / The Field-Reeve's Yard (declaring the bargain) / final ending epilogue
